title: Chicken Cordon Bleu
subtitle: chicken rolled around ham and melty Swiss, baked crisp in buttery panko, with a creamy Parmesan sauce over rice
imageAlt: A sliced golden chicken cordon bleu showing ham and melted Swiss, with creamy sauce and rice on a white plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Have 8 toothpicks ready to hold the rolls closed. Count them in and count them out.
Start the rice first; it's ready when the chicken is.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Pound
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment. Pound each breast between plastic wrap to an even 6 mm. Season with the salt and pepper.

steps.title: Fill and roll
steps.text: Lay a slice of ham and a slice of Swiss on each, folded to fit 1 cm inside the edges. Roll up from a short end and close with 2 toothpicks.

steps.title: Bread
steps.text: Toss the panko with the melted butter. Roll each in the flour, then the beaten eggs, then press into the buttered panko.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake seam side down 25–30 minutes, until golden and the chicken reads 74°C (165°F) in the centre of the meat (not the cheese). Rest 5 minutes and pull out the toothpicks.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: While it bakes, melt the butter in a small pot over medium. Whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the milk and broth. Simmer 3 minutes until thick, then stir in the Parmesan and garlic powder.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Slice each roll in half on an angle and serve over rice with the sauce spooned over.

fixIt.fix: Keep the ham and cheese 1 cm in from the edges and roll tightly; seam side down holds it closed.
Bake on the middle rack, or broil 1 minute at the end, watching closely.
Add the milk slowly while whisking; a minute of hard whisking smooths small lumps.

saleTip: Buy deli ham sliced thin at the counter: you only need 4 slices, so ask for just 100 g.
swap: Air fryer: 2 rolls at a time at 190°C, 18–20 minutes, turning once, to 74°C (165°F).
leftovers: Slice cold for a lunch sandwich, or reheat in the oven so the crumb stays crisp.
doneness: Chicken at 74°C (165°F) in the centre of the meat (Health Canada, poultry pieces).
source: Based on tested baked chicken cordon bleu methods (Canadian Living, America's Test Kitchen): pounded breasts rolled with ham and Swiss, buttered panko crust, baked at 200°C, with a light cheese sauce.
prepAhead: Roll and bread the chicken up to 1 day ahead; keep covered in the fridge.
Freeze breaded raw rolls; bake from thawed.
reheat: At 180°C (350°F) for 15 minutes, until 74°C (165°F). Warm the sauce in a small pot with a splash of milk.

basic.note: Crispy rolls with rice; no sauce.

fancy.note: Garlic butter green beans on the side.

addSteps.title: Green beans
addSteps.text: Boil the beans in salted water 4 minutes, drain, and toss in a hot pan with the butter and garlic for 1 minute.

plating: Rice in a neat mound, the two halves leaning on it cut side up.
Sauce spooned across, not over the crust.

why.0-0: Pounding to an even thickness means the roll cooks through before the crust burns.
why.0-8: Buttered panko browns in the oven like it was fried.
why.0-4: Swiss melts smooth without going greasy, and it's the classic.

funFact: 'Cordon bleu' means 'blue ribbon', after the sash worn by France's highest order of knights; it became a name for top-class cooking.

keeps.note: freeze baked rolls without the sauce
